_comment: Updates compiled from Granola meeting notes for the BRE initiative. epicKeys link an update to one or more epics/initiatives in epics.json (Jira keys).

updates.title: BRE — Sprint status update & Sync contract delay
updates.summary: The Order Integration roadmap, originally set to conclude on June 9, has been pushed. The Sync team shifted their execution from Sprint 193 (May 18) to Sprint 194 (June 1) due to pending dependencies and validation gaps. This moved the BRE implementation to Sprint 195 and extended the delivery timeline to June 23. The EDI MVP Q2 scope now has no contingency margin, increasing delivery risk. Root cause: zones have not yet provided final feedback on the Sync contract. Teams are actively following up.
decisions: Delivery of Order Integration (BEESEDI-48925) extended to June 23 — two weeks later than the original June 9 plan
Risk escalated: no contingency margin remaining for Q2 EDI MVP scope
Zone feedback on the Sync contract is the critical-path unblocking item
actionItems: Pamela / Renan: follow up with MX and AR zones for final Sync contract feedback — blocking Sprint 194 planning
Team: ensure all Sync contract validations are completed before Sprint 194 planning (starts ~June 1)
Pamela: continue reporting the Sync dependency pain point in weekly status updates

updates.title: BRE — Weekly checkpoint (Sprint 93)
updates.summary: Sprint 93 status review. BEESEDI-48925 (Order integration) advanced to SIT Tests after a joint validation session with the Cart Checkout team on May 12. BEESCR-27918 (Cart Service) reached Ready for Prod. BEESEDI-48956 (Purchase number uniqueness) slipped to June 9 due to missed capacity in Sprint 192. BEESIG-13405 (EDI Entity on BEES Sync) moved to In Story Detailing; Sync team contract implementation planned for Sprint 193 starting May 18.
decisions: BEESEDI-48956 delivery date pushed from May 26 to June 9 due to Sprint 192 capacity miss
BEESCR-27918 is Ready for Prod following joint Cart + BRE validation on May 12
Sync contract implementation scheduled for Sprint 193 (May 18) — zones must confirm contract before planning
actionItems: Team: conduct joint validation session outcomes review and close remaining SIT issues on BEESEDI-48925
Pamela: track Sprint 193 Sync contract inclusion and escalate if zones delay feedback

Eric praised the tracker tool and suggested grouping tasks into swim lanes per workstream.
decisions: Pilot 1–2 retailers to validate technical and operational capabilities before scaling 3P EDI
Push commercial / go-to-market strategy for 3P EDI to the commercial team (Jersen and team)
Document the price validation problem (deviations, expected workflows, market variations) before further development assumptions

updates.title: Pack size and order quantity mapping for broker integration
updates.summary: Defined how pack size and quantity should be mapped in broker orders (Quantity ÷ Pack Size = actual units). Evaluated two implementation paths and the budget/timeline route.
decisions: Calculation method confirmed: Quantity ÷ Pack Size = units ordered (current unit field discarded as unreliable)
Two approaches on the table: Azure intermediate component (broker team) vs. direct integration with existing box-to-units logic
actionItems: Update integration documentation to include pack size as a divisor field
Broker team: produce budget estimates after reviewing updated documentation

updates.title: [AR] Order integration assessment
updates.summary: Walkthrough of the JSON integration contract for Argentina, covering the two-stage validation process (format + business rules). Contract structure based on Cricus order examples reviewed end-to-end.
decisions: Contract fields confirmed: PO number, customer account ID, external retailer ID, GTIN, SKU, quantity, base price
Provider field is Mexico-specific; optional for Argentina
actionItems: Resolve open questions on tax calculation method and discount application in the next-day technical meeting
Argentina partner: approve final contract before implementation begins

updates.title: Price control & order validation strategy — supermarkets
updates.summary: Defined the price validation strategy for supermarket chains: chain-specific pricing rules (price only, price+discount, price+discount+taxes), tolerance thresholds, and the manual review workflow for out-of-tolerance orders.
decisions: Price tolerance set at chain level: 1% default; 0.1% or 0% for chains with bad credit history
Manual OTC review process (SKU-by-SKU) with a 24h SLA to prevent backlog
Empties / bottle returns excluded from price validation scope
actionItems: Schedule a meeting with Cricos to clarify the discount field
Specify a front-end review portal to replace the Excel + CRM workflow

updates.title: Delivery rules available in BEES — Platform deep-dive
updates.summary: Deep-dive with the BEES Platform team on the unified delivery rules system. Reviewed the consolidation of delivery window and delivery range concepts and how the new system handles per-account/network granularity.
decisions: Delivery window and delivery range are now unified in a single system; legacy CDD-based configs still active for MX/AR
New system supports per-account / per-network granularity (e.g., Oxxo D+3 vs. other networks D+2)
actionItems: Investigate whether MX and AR are still consuming CDD data
Verify implementation status of the unified delivery rules in both zones

updates.title: Delivery rules review with Mexico
updates.summary: Reviewed Mexico's two core delivery validation rules — delivery range (minimum lead time per retailer) and delivery frequency (authorized delivery windows). Clarified the SEDIS vs. PDC order-type distinction and its impact on rule application.
decisions: Delivery range rule: minimum 1 day (OXXO) to 2 days (Extra), with cutoff time enforcement
Delivery frequency rule: candidate to be postponed to 2027 — 40% of orders would be blocked today
actionItems: Jason: confirm which order field carries the expiration date and assess complexity of the frequency rule
Resolve SEDIS vs. PDC distinction before enforcing the frequency rule

Stories were built from existing HLRs and split into 4 main epics with granular stories per team (mobile, backend, frontend) for parallel execution. Resourcing risks discussed (only 2 BE + 2 FE devs, headcount gap analyzed with NTT).

Reuse 2 existing BI team services in the solution
David Quirino confirmed as internal addition to the team

updates.title: Alignment with Cart team
updates.summary: Finalized Argentina 2026 scope, covering UPC matching, delivery range validation, expiration date logic, and the complexity of price-with-tax validation. Several open items flagged for follow-up with the Argentina team.
decisions: Drop the 'holding cell' for unmatched UPC orders for 2026 — too complex; replace with visibility on lost orders + manual curation
Many-to-many UPC/SKU relationships required; SKU selection based on healthiest stock
Expiration date defaults to 15 days when not specified in the EDI

updates.title: BRE HLS presentation
updates.summary: High-level solution presentation covering BRE system architecture, validation rules, and Q2 development plan. Discussed Kafka vs. direct API for JSON ingestion and reuse vs. duplication of existing system components.
decisions: MVP scoped to JSON input; later expansion to PDF, XLS, and other formats
Q2 priority order: POC identification → product validations → price validations
Architecture must be extensible for 3P (third-party) formats
actionItems: Decide Kafka vs. direct API once flexibility requirements are clear
Talk to Marcel about technical dependencies
Update architecture diagram with 3P options
Evaluate reusable components from the current system

updates.title: Checkpoint — long-term EDI vision & JSON contract
updates.summary: Strategic session covering the long-term EDI vision (BEES as a marketplace replacing legacy networks like Farmalink, NowGrid, iCube) and a deep review of the JSON integration contract structure: provider number, account number, dates, totals, SKU, CDD. L'Oréal wants to decommission their current tool and migrate 100% to BEES.
decisions: Phased EDI rollout: focus on 2–3 EDI patterns for Q2 (X12, EDIFACT, Swift, Rosetta Net, SAP); expand gradually to 20+
CDD field optional in JSON contract (mandatory for Argentina, optional for Mexico)
Currency / payment fields belong inside the JSON payload (per-order), not in static configuration
Code mapping responsibility: zones provide client-code → BEES customer-account-ID mapping; BEES handles the lookup
Argentina & Mexico: run BEES in parallel with existing systems through early 2027; replace if performance is superior
actionItems: Renan: map retail networks, their technical maturity and integration capabilities (JSON vs SFTP/TXT)
Renan: validate whether BRE business rules are sufficient for pharmacy networks (farmácias)
Renan: review and validate the JSON contract draft when received
Architecture team: define solution components for the long-term vision vs Q2 delivery
Renan: be included in 3P discovery discussions for broader strategic context

updates.summary: Strategic 1:1 covering BRE delivery progress, EDI integration strategy, and the broader BEES marketplace vision (industries, distributors, retail networks — potentially replacing Farmalink-type players). Discussed the 'why route through BRE vs. directly to the system' question and the need for retrocompatibility with existing tools.
decisions: Architecture team owns the justification for routing through BRE (not Renan or Tanaka)
Build a retrocompatible EDI solution with a clear deprecation path for legacy integrations
Prioritize a native-connector strategy to ease network migration

Heraldo to bridge Guilherme with the product team for continuity
